author: Kittlitz, 1830
status: 텃새 수만 마리 · 겨울철새 수백 마리
habitat: 남해안과 서남해 섬의 덤불과 숲 가장자리, 대숲, 높은 산의 관목 덤불
summary: 남해안과 서남해·서해의 섬에서 흔히 번식하는 텃새로, 전라남도에서 강원도까지 본토 높은 산의 관목 덤불에서도 여름에 번식한다. 덤불 속에 숨어 지내 모습보다 '찻, 찻' 하는 소리로 알아차리는 일이 많고, 수컷은 봄부터 '호-호케쿄' 하고 크게 지저귄다. 주로 곤충과 거미를 먹으며, 둥지 짓기와 알 품기, 새끼 기르기는 모두 암컷이 맡고 수컷 한 마리가 여러 암컷과 짝을 짓기도 한다. 국외에서는 일본과 사할린 남부에서 번식한다.

sexes.text: 암수 생김새가 같고, 수컷이 암컷보다 눈에 띄게 크다.

similar.how: 휘파람새는 몸이 더 크고 이마와 정수리가 붉은 갈색을 띠며, 주로 4~10월에 보인다.

art.subject: Japanese Bush Warbler (Horornis diphone), adult male, as seen on southern Korean islands in spring: upperparts plain olive-brown to greyish olive without any streaks; faint pale buff-white supercilium; dusky eye-stripe; wings plain olive-brown with no wing-bars; underparts dull whitish, washed grey-buff on the breast sides and flanks; tail plain olive-brown, fairly long and rounded. Bill fine and pointed, dark brown above with a paler pinkish lower mandible. Dark eye. Pinkish legs.
art.pose: singing from an open twig at the edge of a dense evergreen shrub, head raised and bill open, side view
art.scene: dense evergreen camellia and bamboo thicket on a southern Korean island such as Jeju in spring, dappled light; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male, side view perched at the edge of a thicket: plain olive-brown upperparts and wings with no streaks or wing-bars, faint pale buff-white supercilium over a dusky eye-stripe, dull whitish underparts washed grey-buff on the breast sides and flanks, short rounded wings, fairly long, rounded plain olive-brown tail, pinkish legs

adult male, head detail in profile: rounded head with the crown feathers lying flat and no crest, faint pale buff-white supercilium and dusky eye-stripe, short, fine pointed bill dark brown above with a paler pinkish lower mandible, dark eye
art.build: Small, plain, skulking bush warbler, about the size of a sparrow, males noticeably larger than females; rounded head with no crest, the crown feathers lying flat; plump body and a fairly long, rounded tail. Bill short, thin and pointed. Legs fairly long and sturdy, pinkish. Wings short and rounded, the wingtips reaching only the base of the tail. Stays inside dense evergreen and bamboo thickets; sings with the head raised.
avoid: Do not add wing-bars, streaks or spots; the plumage is plain olive-brown.
Do not paint yellow or green-tinged underparts like a leaf warbler.
Do not paint a bold white supercilium and black eye-stripe; the face pattern is soft and faint.
Do not paint a short, stubby tail; it is fairly long and rounded.
